root_cause.text: In fs/smb/client, struct cached_fid stored multiple independently updated state flags as bitfields in the same byte, so concurrent bitfield writes performed byte-level read-modify-write operations that could overwrite each other and reintroduce stale flag values.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE and commit explicitly state that “is_open, has_lease and on_list are stored in the same bitfield byte in struct cached_fid” and that “bitfield assignments generate byte read–modify–write operations,” with the shown CPU interleaving demonstrating stale bits being restored; the patch fixes this by replacing the bitfields `bool has_lease:1`, `bool is_open:1`, `bool on_list:1`, and `bool file_all_info_is_valid:1` with separate `bool` fields.

intent_record.intent_summary: Replace cached_fid boolean bitfields with plain bool members to simplify flag storage without changing intended semantics.
intent_record.what: The four boolean fields in struct cached_fid—has_lease, is_open, on_list, and file_all_info_is_valid—were changed from 1-bit bitfield declarations (bool field:1) to plain bool members.
intent_record.how: At runtime, these fields are now stored as normal boolean members instead of packed bitfields, which changes the struct layout and avoids bitfield-specific access and representation behavior while preserving the same true/false semantics for the flags.

grouping_result.intent: Replace cached_fid boolean bitfields with plain bool members to simplify flag storage without changing intended semantics.

relevance_review.reason: The vulnerability is caused by multiple independently updated state flags being stored as bitfields in the same byte, leading to racy read-modify-write behavior. Replacing those cached_fid bitfields with plain bool members directly removes that shared-byte bitfield storage and addresses the root cause.

bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet is sufficient because the root cause is specifically about how `struct cached_fid` stores multiple independently updated flags, and the full relevant declaration is shown here. The vulnerable construct is present: lines 34-36 declare three separate 1-bit `bool` bitfields in the same struct storage unit: `bool is_valid:1;`, `bool file_all_info_is_valid:1;`, and `bool has_lease:1;`. This matches the root cause exactly: independently updated state flags are represented as bitfields packed into the same byte/storage unit, so concurrent updates can perform read-modify-write on the shared byte and overwrite each other. There is no indication of the fix here, such as converting these flags to separate full-width fields/bytes or another representation that avoids shared-byte bitfield RMW races. Therefore this version contains the bug and does not yet contain the fix.
